props.title: The Craft
props.initialSlug: Be careful what you witch for

sections.content: The Craft revolutionized teen supernatural horror by blending authentic Wiccan elements with high school drama. Like Carrie (1976) before it, the film taps into female adolescent power dynamics, but director Andrew Fleming takes it further by exploring how marginalized teens might actually embrace and weaponize their outsider status. The film's influence echoes through later teen witch narratives like Charmed (1998) and The Blair Witch Project (1999), establishing a template for how modern horror could tackle themes of female empowerment and corruption.

sections.content: The film's aesthetic influence can't be overstated. Costume designer Deborah Everton created an iconic "witch grunge" look that defined 90s alternative fashion. The quartet's transformation from outcasts to powerful coven members inspired countless horror-fashion crossovers, visible in everything from Jennifer's Body (2009) to The Craft: Legacy (2020). The film's visual approach to depicting magic - practical effects mixed with subtle CGI - set a standard that many supernatural films still reference.

What makes The Craft particularly significant is its treatment of power dynamics and consequences. Unlike lighter witch fare like Hocus Pocus (1993), the film takes its occult elements seriously, showing both the allure and danger of unchecked power. This approach influenced later works like American Horror Story: Coven (2013) and Chilling Adventures of Sabrina (2018), where witchcraft serves as a metaphor for female agency in patriarchal systems. sections.content: The Craft marked a crucial shift in teen horror, moving away from pure slasher narratives toward more complex supernatural threats. This paved the way for films like Ginger Snaps (2000) and May (2002), which used horror elements to explore female coming-of-age stories. The film's success proved audiences were ready for horror that tackled serious themes while maintaining commercial appeal.
